name: Agriculture
blurb: Vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, and autonomous equipment at commercial scale, tracked through USDA ERS, FAO, satellite data providers, and the equipment and standards bodies.

points.desc: Deere's precision agriculture line (See and Spray, autonomous tractors) is the reference commercial deployment.
points.name: Precision ag is shipping product

points.desc: Census BTOS covers agriculture-adjacent sectors in its fortnightly AI-use series.
points.name: Adoption is measured, not guessed

points.desc: The Economic Research Service publishes the data series on precision-agriculture adoption across US farms - variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, autonomous equipment. The federal measurement layer.
points.name: USDA ERS measures US adoption

points.desc: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization's digital agriculture program, with the 60 Decibels-supported Digital Agriculture Index, benchmarks platform adoption and real-world yield and income impact.
points.name: FAO benchmarks digital agriculture globally

points.desc: The AgriFoodTech investment research tracks venture capital into agricultural AI, robotics, computer vision, and farm-management software - the sector's funding barometer.
points.name: AgFunder indexes the investment flow

points.desc: Planet Labs' high-resolution imagery, Descartes Labs' geospatial ML, and EarthDaily's field-level crop indicators supply the AI-ready observation data behind yield prediction and crop-stress detection.
points.name: The satellite layer feeds the models

points.desc: The Association of Equipment Manufacturers covers autonomous machinery, AI hardware standards, and robotics adoption across crop and livestock production.
points.name: AEM tracks the machinery standards

points.desc: The nonprofit consortium sets the open data standards that let AI models ingest feeds from tractors, drones, soil sensors, and satellites - the plumbing under everything else.
points.name: AgGateway makes the data interoperable

points.desc: The International Society of Precision Agriculture is the scientific organization connecting academic research on remote sensing and spatial analytics to commercial practice.
points.name: ISPA bridges the science and the field

points.desc: The 100 Million Farmers initiative tracks AI adoption through the lens of climate-smart and regenerative agriculture metrics globally.
points.name: WEF tracks climate-smart adoption

points.desc: Bayer's Climate FieldView and Corteva's Granular are the large digital-farming platforms turning soil, weather, and yield data into planting and input prescriptions with machine learning.
points.name: The agribusiness platforms run the prescriptions

points.desc: CNH Industrial's Raven division builds driverless tractor technology, AI path-planning, and precision application - the equipment layer beyond Deere.
points.name: CNH and Raven automate the other fleets

points.desc: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder kills weeds with computer vision and lasers instead of herbicide; Monarch builds electric driverless tractors - narrow AI shipping as farm equipment.
points.name: The pure-plays attack single problems

summary: Precision agriculture - vision-guided spraying, yield prediction, autonomous equipment - is deployed at commercial scale. Who tracks it: federal adoption data, a UN benchmarking framework, a venture index, and standards bodies, layered over the equipment giants and AI pure-plays actually shipping it.

analysis.body:
Agriculture sits at 13.7 percent of firms reporting active AI use in the Census Bureau's Business Trends and Business Outlook Survey, a figure that reflects the sector's uneven digitization: large commercial operations are running sophisticated systems while much of the industry remains at an earlier stage. The prior period figure was suppressed, so the direction of travel cannot be confirmed from that comparison alone, but the current reading places agriculture in the measurable tier of AI-adopting industries rather than at either extreme.

Where the money and vendors concentrate is fairly clear from the documented deployments. Deere's See and Spray and autonomous tractor lines represent the reference commercial deployment for vision-guided, in-field AI, while CNH Industrial's Raven division builds competing driverless tractor technology and AI path-planning for equipment fleets beyond Deere's customer base. At the platform layer, Bayer's Climate FieldView and Corteva's Granular are the dominant digital-farming systems, ingesting soil, weather, and yield data to generate machine-learning-derived planting and input prescriptions at scale. Narrower pure-play entrants are also shipping product: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder uses computer vision and lasers to eliminate weeds without herbicide, and Monarch Tractor builds electric driverless equipment aimed at smaller operations. The observation layer feeding all of these systems runs through Planet Labs' high-resolution satellite imagery, Descartes Labs' geospatial machine learning, and EarthDaily's field-level crop-stress indicators, with data interoperability governed by the open standards maintained by AgGateway.

The measurement and standards infrastructure is more developed than in many sectors. USDA's Economic Research Service tracks precision-agriculture adoption across variable-rate technology, yield monitoring, and autonomous equipment, giving the industry a federal baseline. The FAO's Digital Agriculture Index, supported by 60 Decibels, benchmarks platform adoption and real-world yield and income impact globally, while the World Economic Forum's 100 Million Farmers initiative layers in climate-smart and regenerative agriculture metrics. The Association of Equipment Manufacturers covers autonomous machinery and AI hardware standards, and the International Society of Precision Agriculture connects academic remote-sensing research to commercial practice. This density of standards bodies and measurement organizations is a meaningful structural advantage for buyers trying to evaluate vendors against documented outcomes rather than marketing claims.

For anyone deciding whether to deploy, the picture is that the technology at the equipment and platform tier is commercially mature and independently measured, not experimental. The risks that remain are interoperability, since AgGateway's open standards work is ongoing rather than complete, and the data access question of whether a given operation generates the volume and quality of field observations that these models require to produce reliable prescriptions. Smaller and less-capitalized farms are likely to find the platform economics and connectivity requirements a genuine barrier, while large row-crop operations are already inside the documented deployment perimeter. Buyers should verify that any vendor's yield-prediction or application-prescription claims rest on outcomes tracked by USDA ERS or equivalent independent measurement, not solely on proprietary trial data.
